notes: Canonical injection/exfil pattern set. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the TS write-time scanner (src/index.ts scanContent) and the Python retro-scanner (injection_scan.py). Patterns are written in a dialect both JS RegExp and Python re accept — avoid lookbehind, named groups and \p{...} classes. BUMP `version` on ANY change to `patterns`: memory-injection-rescan.timer re-scans every row whose memories.scan_pattern_version is behind this number, which is what makes pattern additions retroactive instead of forward-only.

mode_meaning.block: scanContent() rejects the write. Mirrors the hard-block arm of the scan_memory_for_injection() DB trigger (migration 076).
mode_meaning.signal: Does NOT block. The DB trigger stores the row but caps trust_tier at 'quarantined' (recall weight 0.40). scanContent() ignores these — the TS layer has never blocked on them and must not start, or every existing signal-only row becomes unwritable. injection_scan.py DOES scan them, because they are the arm that actually quarantines and the 785 pre-076 rows were never checked against it either.

severity_meaning.high: No legitimate reason for this text to sit in a memory row. Treat a finding as probable poisoning.
severity_meaning.medium: Attack-shaped but expressible in ordinary technical writing. Read the excerpt before acting.
severity_meaning.low: Dual-use in a homelab corpus — az-lab genuinely documents SSH keys, .env files and credential paths. Expect a high benign rate; these exist to make exfil TEXT visible, not to accuse.

parity_notes: Verified against pg_get_functiondef(scan_memory_for_injection) on 2026-08-02. Two intentional asymmetries, recorded here so nobody 'fixes' them by accident: (1) ssh_access (~/.ssh) is in the TS list but NOT in the DB trigger's hard block — it matches az-lab's own SSH bootstrap docs, so blocking on it at the DB layer would reject legitimate writes. (2) The five signal patterns are in the DB trigger but NOT in scanContent(). Both layers are represented below; `mode` is what keeps them apart.
